chapter: Rhythm Club memories and playing technique
title: Dick Fulbright, the bass player who lent money

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Oh yes, oh yes. Another name that brought back very fond memories was Fulbright.
Yes, bass player. I worked opposite him at the Savoy Ballroom, he was with Teddy Hill's band.
He was one of the best bass players of the day, right?

Oh yeah. Tell you something about Fulbright. All the musicians knew Fulbright very well, he was a business man, I would say. He used to lend the guys money in the band. If you borrowed five dollars, I forget the
percentage, five dollars on the end of the week, you'd give him six dollars for it. If it was ten dollars, you'd give him two dollars for it at the end of the week.
Kind of a friendly loan shark.

Yeah, oh yeah. And the guys you used to always get Fulbright, well I have to see Fulbright tonight, they'd go on up you know, and Fulbright lend me a ten. First thing Fulbright would say Okay now you have to give me twelve at the end of the week, and he'd be right there when you got paid off and you'd give it to him, and it was a good deal because a lot of guys used to get broke about the middle of the week, you know, and Fulbright was right there, and there wasn't any qualms about it, he'd lend it to you, especially if you paid him back. A lot of guys were a little delinquent in paying, if they told him I'll pay you back the end of the week, they may not pay him back for another two weeks, and then they'd add fifty cents more onto it, and then the longer it would go, you know, the longer they would be to pay off.
I take it he didn't get burned very often.

No, no he didn't, because he was right on you every time. Well he knew the guys that he could trust, you know, and really depend on to pay him back. Fulbright was a great guy. He brought back some memories. Very nice personality playing his bass. Did you ever see him play?
